description.narrative: The IDF Grant would be the first step in a long-term capacity building program for improving public expenditure management in agriculture. It would focus on designing a COFOG-based expenditure classification system able to support the sufficiently detailed allocation, reporting and tracking of national public expenditures in the agricultural sector. Activities to be supported by the Grant. Component 1: Stocktaking/inventory of current accounting and reporting practices in about 4 countries in Southern and West Africa and identification of steps and resources necessary for full adoption of COFOG. Component 2: Establishment of a capacity in the NEPAD Secretariat for advocacy by the NEPAD Secretariat for the adoption of COFOG classification and for assisting member countries during implementation, including ensuring that all interested member countries learn and benefit from the pilots that will be conducted under this Grant. Component 3 Development of an improved COFOG classification able to meet member country requirements for tracking public expenditures targeting, quality and levels. Expected outcomes include (i) the design and testing of an improved COFOG system for allocating, recording and tracking public expenditures in the rural sector; (ii) the sequencing, implementation plan and cost estimates for a country to implement a switch to the improved COFOG system; and (iii) increased capacity at the NEPAD Secretariat to provide leadership, guidance and implementation support for African countries to adopt the system. To support the New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD) Secretariat and African governments in long-term capacity building for improving public expenditure tracking in agriculture, forestry, and fisheries.
